chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Abū Jamīlah, from Muḥammad al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
Indeed, Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله said: “Indeed, Allah represented my community to me in the clay and taught me their names just as He taught Ādam the names, all of them.”
“Then the أصحابُ الرَّايَات passed by me, so I sought forgiveness for ʿAlī and his Shīʿah.”
“Indeed, my Lord promised me, concerning the Shīʿah of ʿAlī, a special quality.”

It was said, “O Rasūl Allāh, and what is it?” He said: “Forgiveness for those among them who believe, and that neither a minor sin nor a major sin of theirs will be left, and for them evil deeds will be changed into good deeds.”

key_terms.أَسْمَاءَهُمْ: their names, taught by Allah to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.أَصْحَابُ الرَّايَاتِ: the أصحاب of the banners who passed by him
key_terms.السَّيِّئَاتُ: evil deeds that are changed into good deeds
key_terms.الطِّينِ: the clay in which the community was represented to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.الْمَغْفِرَةُ: divine forgiveness promised for the believers among them
key_terms.شِيعَتِهِ: his Shīʿah, referring here to the followers of ʿAlī عليه السلام

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the forgiveness promised for the believing Shīʿah of ʿAlī عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith describes a divinely granted knowledge given to Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله regarding his community, including their identities, and highlights his seeking forgiveness for ʿAlī عليه السلام and his Shīʿah. It emphasizes divine forgiveness for the believing Shīʿah of ʿAlī عليه السلام, including the transformation of their evil deeds into good deeds.

en.hubeali:
A nmber of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abu Jameela, from Muhammad Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Made a resemblance of my<sup>saww</sup> community for me<sup>saww</sup> in the clay and Taught me<sup>saww</sup> their names just as He<sup>azwj</sup> had Taught Adam<sup>saww</sup> the names, all of them.
So the owners of the flags passed by me<sup>saww</sup>, and they sought Forgiveness for Ali<sup>asws</sup> and his<sup>asws</sup> Shias.
My<sup>saww</sup> Lord<sup>azwj</sup> Promised me<sup>saww</sup> a characteristic with regards to the Shias of Ali<sup>asws</sup>’.

It was said, ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! And what is it?’ He<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The Forgiveness for the ones from them who believe and that neither a minor (sin) nor a major (sin) of theirs would be left, and the evil deeds would be changed to good deeds’.
en.sarwar: 14. A number of our people has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Sayf from ‘Amr ibn Shimr from Jabir who has said the following. “I asked abu Ja‘far (a.s.), ‘describe to me the Prophet (s.a) of Allah.”

The Imam (a.s.) said, “The Holy Prophet (s.a) has a white reddish complexion, large balck eyes, the eyebrows almost joined, chubby hands and feet as if gold molded as to the form of his fingers and toes and with manifest shoulder bones. When he would turn to a person he would so with the whole of his body. Due to kind and tender heartiness. A line of hair extended from the front cavity of his neck down to his bellybutton as if it was a clear and pure silver lining. His neck was tall and clear, his nose would almost touch the water when he wanted to drink and when walking he would somehow lean forwards as if walking on a downward slope. No one similar to him was seen before or after the Holy Prophet (s.a) of Allah.”
